output.name: Hálmet — the Knotted Tail
output.myth: Aun cut the string because he wanted to know how far the wind went. The sky drifted off with him holding the knife, and every kite he had flown on that string went up after it. Ennu made the first of them from sailcloth and whale-rib, and when it broke loose it sailed up with no hand on it. That is Varesk. Its belly holds the bright sail-star, and its tail hangs down toward the sea, because a tail is the part the wind can hold. Tavo the Gale laughed and would not give it back. Ránu, to the west, has Aun's ribbon streaming off behind, and says it is untidy. Hovan keeps watch from the north, where a boat's name was painted in red ochre and then lost. Mother Hesk found one string short and counts it every night. Fishermen tie a knot in their cords for each boat they lose, so Hesk can find them. Those knots hang from Varesk's tail. Aun is said to fly it still, slow in the dark, waiting for someone on the islands to take up the cut end and pull.
output.finding: Find Ránu, the Sun-Kite's Ribbon, on the Lamp Road, then look about one hand-span (roughly 20°) east of it for Varesk, the kite whose tail hangs down toward the sea.
